section_1_prerequisites.title: Prerequisite Check: The Slope and the Area
section_1_prerequisites.content: Briefly revisit two core geometric ideas: 1. Slope (steepness of a line) and 2. Area (space inside a shape). Establish that Calculus is just the study of these two ideas applied to curves instead of straight lines. Use a simple line graph to show these concepts side-by-side.
section_1_prerequisites.example: Visualize a Snail climbing a hill. The 'Steepness' is how hard the snail works at a single point; the 'Total Grass Eaten' is the area of the field the snail covered.

section_2_derivative.title: The Derivative: Zooming into 'The Now'
section_2_derivative.content: Define the derivative as the instantaneous rate of change. Explain that by 'zooming in' infinitely on a curve, it looks like a straight line. The derivative tells us the slope of that line at any specific moment (x). Highlight the notation f'(x).
section_2_derivative.example: A Race Car's speedometer. At exactly 2.5 seconds, the needle points to 60 km/h. That single snapshot of speed is the derivative of the car's position.

section_3_integral.title: The Integral: Accumulating the 'Whole'
section_3_integral.content: Define the definite integral as the total accumulation or the 'Area Under the Curve'. Explain the process of 'Slicing': dividing a complex shape into infinitely many thin rectangles and summing them up. Highlight the notation ∫ f(x) dx.
section_3_integral.example: A Rain Gauge collecting water. If the rain falls at different rates (the curve), the total water in the bucket at the end of the hour is the integral of the rainfall rate.

section_4_connection.title: The Fundamental Theorem: The 'Undo' Button
section_4_connection.content: Reveal the core secret: Differentiation and Integration are inverse operations, like adding and subtracting. If you have a function representing total distance, its derivative is speed. If you have a function representing speed, its integral is the distance. Graphically, show how the 'area-so-far' function grows based on the height of the original curve.
section_4_connection.example: A 3D Printer. The derivative is the 'Extruder' nozzle speed at a specific layer; the integral is the 'Finished Model' created by the accumulation of all those layers.

section_5_synthesis.title: Visual Synthesis & Animation
section_5_synthesis.content: Animate a point moving along a curve. Simultaneously show two graphs: one tracking the 'Slope' (Derivative) and one filling in the 'Area' (Integral). Demonstrate that the 'Slope' of the Area graph is equal to the 'Height' of the original graph.
section_5_synthesis.example: A 'Balloon Character' inflating. The 'Rate of Air Flow' (Derivative) determines how fast the 'Volume' (Integral) increases. If the flow stops (Derivative = 0), the volume stays constant (Integral curve becomes a flat line).

Establish that Calculus is just the study of these two ideas applied to curves instead of straight lines. Use a simple line graph to show these concepts side-by-side.
section_1_prerequisites.example: Visualize a Snail climbing a hill. The 'Steepness' is how hard the snail works at a single point; the 'Total Grass Eaten' is the area of the field the snail covered.

section_2_derivative.title: The Derivative: Zooming into 'The Now'
section_2_derivative.content: Define the derivative as the instantaneous rate of change. Explain that by 'zooming in' infinitely on a curve, it looks like a straight line. The derivative tells us the slope of that line at any specific moment (x). Highlight the notation f'(x).
section_2_derivative.example: A Race Car's speedometer. At exactly 2.5 seconds, the needle points to 60 km/h. That single snapshot of speed is the derivative of the car's position.

section_3_integral.title: The Integral: Accumulating the 'Whole'
section_3_integral.content: Define the definite integral as the total accumulation or the 'Area Under the Curve'. Explain the process of 'Slicing': dividing a complex shape into infinitely many thin rectangles and summing them up. Highlight the notation ∫ f(x) dx.
section_3_integral.example: A Rain Gauge collecting water. If the rain falls at different rates (the curve), the total water in the bucket at the end of the hour is the integral of the rainfall rate.

section_4_connection.title: The Fundamental Theorem: The 'Undo' Button
section_4_connection.content: Reveal the core secret: Differentiation and Integration are inverse operations, like adding and subtracting. If you have a function representing total distance, its derivative is speed. If you have a function representing speed, its integral is the distance. Graphically, show how the 'area-so-far' function grows based on the height of the original curve.
section_4_connection.example: A 3D Printer. The derivative is the 'Extruder' nozzle speed at a specific layer; the integral is the 'Finished Model' created by the accumulation of all those layers.

section_5_synthesis.title: Visual Synthesis & Animation
section_5_synthesis.content: Animate a point moving along a curve. Simultaneously show two graphs: one tracking the 'Slope' (Derivative) and one filling in the 'Area' (Integral). Demonstrate that the 'Slope' of the Area graph is equal to the 'Height' of the original graph.
section_5_synthesis.example: A 'Balloon Character' inflating. The 'Rate of Air Flow' (Derivative) determines how fast the 'Volume' (Integral) increases. If the flow stops (Derivative = 0), the volume stays constant (Integral curve becomes a flat line).

section_1_prerequisites.title: Prerequisite Check: The Slope and the Area
lecture_lines: Calculus studies slope and area applied to curves.
Slope measures the steepness at a single point.
Area measures the space accumulated under the curve.
animations: Show a snail (#FFFFFF) on a hill curve (#00FF00). Highlight a tangent line (#FFD700) showing 'Steepness'.
Fill the area under the hill curve with a light green color (#90EE90) to represent 'Total Grass Eaten'.
Side-by-side comparison: Label the tangent 'Slope' (#FFD700) and the filled region 'Area' (#90EE90).

section_2_derivative.title: The Derivative: Zooming into 'The Now'
lecture_lines: A derivative represents the instantaneous rate of change.
Zoom into a curve until it looks straight.
This straight line's slope is the derivative f'(x).
Like a speedometer showing speed at one moment.
It captures the precise "steepness of the now."
animations: Display a race car (#FFFFFF) moving along a position curve (#00BFFF).
Place a point on the curve at t=2.5. Display a speedometer (#FF4500) pointing to 60 km/h.
Zoom in on the point at t=2.5 until the curve looks like a straight line (#FFFF00).
Highlight the slope of this line and label it f'(2.5) = 60 (#FFD700).
Fade out the zoom and car; show the general notation f'(x) (#FFFFFF) next to the curve.

section_3_integral.title: The Integral: Accumulating the 'Whole'
lecture_lines: An integral calculates the total accumulation over time.
We slice the area into many thin rectangles.
Summing these rectangles gives the total area.
Notation \int f(x) dx represents this infinite sum.
It is like a rain gauge collecting every drop.
animations: Show a rain cloud (#87CEEB) above a rain gauge (#C0C0C0). A curve (#4169E1) represents rainfall rate.
Divide the area under the rainfall curve into thick vertical rectangles (#ADD8E6).
Increase the number of rectangles while making them thinner, filling the area more precisely.
Gradually fill the rain gauge (#C0C0C0) with 'water' (#1E90FF) as the rectangles accumulate.
Label the total water in the gauge as the integral f(x) dx (#FFFFFF).

section_4_connection.title: The Fundamental Theorem: The 'Undo' Button
lecture_lines: Differentiation and integration are inverse operations.
One "undoes" the other, like adding and subtracting.
The derivative of distance is your current speed.
The integral of speed is your total distance.
This link is the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus.
animations: Show a 3D printer nozzle (#C0C0C0) moving across a layer. Label its speed as 'Derivative' (#FF8C00).
Show the finished model (#32CD32) growing layer by layer. Label the total model as 'Integral' (#00FA9A).
Display a 'Distance' graph (#FFFFFF) and a 'Speed' graph (#FFD700) stacked vertically.
Animate a point on the Speed graph; show the corresponding Slope of the Distance graph changing.
Display a large 'UNDO' button icon (#FF0000) between the symbols d/dx and integral.

section_5_synthesis.title: Visual Synthesis & Animation
lecture_lines: The slope of the area graph matches the height.
Watch the rate of change and accumulation unite.
The Great Loop of Calculus is now complete.
animations: Show a balloon character (#FF69B4) inflating. Display an 'Air Flow Rate' gauge (#00FF00).
Animate the balloon's volume increasing while simultaneously drawing its 'Volume' curve (#FFB6C1).
Highlight that the Slope of the Volume curve matches the 'Air Flow Rate' at each point.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2DerivativeScene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout(
            "The Derivative: Zooming into 'The Now'",
            [
                "A derivative represents the instantaneous rate of change.",
                "Zoom into a curve until it looks straight.",
                "This straight line's slope is the derivative f'(x).",
                "Like a speedometer showing speed at one moment.",
                "It captures the precise \"steepness of the now.\""
            ]
        )

        # Colors
        COLOR_CAR = "#FFFFFF"
        COLOR_CURVE = "#00BFFF"
        COLOR_SPEEDO = "#FF4500"
        COLOR_TANGENT = "#FFFF00"
        COLOR_SLOPE = "#FFD700"
        COLOR_TEXT = "#FFFFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # A derivative represents the instantaneous rate of change.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_CURVE)
        
        # Create Axes and Curve
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 5, 1],
            y_range=[0, 10, 2],
            x_length=4.5,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": GREY}
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B1", "F6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Position curve: s(t) = 0.4 * t^2

        )

            "We slice the area into many thin rectangles.",
            "Summing these rectangles gives the total area.",
            "Notation \\int f(x) dx represents this infinite sum.",
            "It is like a rain gauge collecting every drop."
        ]

        )
        self.play(Transform(rects_thick, rects_thin))
        self.wait(1)

        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Notation

        self.play(Write(notation))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Water fill
        water = Rectangle(
            height=0.1, width=0.9, 
            fill_color=WATER_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.9, 
            stroke_width=0
        ).move_to(gauge_rect.get_bottom(), aligned_edge=DOWN).shift(UP*0.05)
        
        area_fill = axes.get_area(curve, x_range=[0.5, 4.0], color=WATER_COLOR, opacity=0.4)
        
        # Integral label near gauge

        self.place_at_grid(integral_val_label, "D5", scale_factor=0.8)

            Write(integral_val_label),
            run_time=3
        )

        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

                x = 0.5 + j * 1

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])

        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)

            "Differentiation and integration are inverse operations.",
            "One \"undoes\" the other, like adding and subtracting.",
            "The derivative of distance is your current speed.",
            "The integral of speed is your total distance.",
            "This link is the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus."

        deriv_sym = MathTex(r"\frac{d}{dx}", color=COLOR_DERIVATIVE)
        integ_sym = MathTex(r"\int", color=COLOR_INTEGRAL)
        
        self.place_at_grid(deriv_sym, "A2", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.place_at_grid(integ_sym, "C2", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(deriv_sym), FadeIn(integ_sym))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        undo_box = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, height=0.6, width=1.2, color=COLOR_UNDO, fill_opacity=0.3)
        undo_text = Text("UNDO", font_size=18, color=COLOR_UNDO)
        undo_button = VGroup(undo_box, undo_text)
        self.place_at_grid(undo_button, "B2", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        plus_minus = MathTex(r"+ \longleftrightarrow -", font_size=30, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(plus_minus, "D2", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(undo_button))
        self.play(Write(plus_minus))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(plus_minus))

        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Symbols stay but fade slightly
        self.play(VGroup(deriv_sym, integ_sym, undo_button).animate.set_opacity(0.3))

        # Graphs
        dist_axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[0, 4, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": False},

            val = tracker.get_value()
            slope = val / 2 # Derivative of x^2/4 is x/2

        speed_dot = Dot(color=COLOR_SPEED)
        speed_dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(speed_axes.c2p(tracker.get_value(), tracker.get_value()/2)))
        
        self.add(slope_line, speed_dot)

            run_time=4, 
            rate_func=linear
        )
        slope_line.clear_updaters()
        speed_dot.clear_updaters()
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Finished Model (Integral)
        model_base = Line(LEFT, RIGHT, color=GREY).scale(0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(model_base, "F2", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        model_rect = Rectangle(height=0.01, width=1.0, color=COLOR_MODEL, fill_opacity=0.8)
        model_rect.move_to(model_base.get_center(), aligned_edge=DOWN)
        
        model_label = Text("Model (Integral)", font_size=16, color=COLOR_INTEGRAL)
        self.place_at_grid(model_label, "F3", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(Create(model_base), FadeIn(model_label), Create(model_rect))
        
        # Growth animation
        tracker.set_value(0.01)
        model_rect.add_updater(lambda m: m.set_height(max(0.01, tracker.get_value() * 0.4), stretch=True).move_to(model_base.get_center(), aligned_edge=DOWN))
        
        self.play(Create(area), tracker.animate.set_value(4), run_time=3)
        model_rect.clear_updaters()
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        ftc_text = Text("Fundamental Theorem of Calculus", font_size=24, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_in_area(ftc_text, "B2", "C5", scale_factor=0.9)
        ftc_box = SurroundingRectangle(ftc_text, color=YELLOW, buff=0.2)

from manim import *

    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)

        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5SynthesisScene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initial Setup
        title = "Visual Synthesis & Animation"
        lecture_lines = [
            "The slope of the area graph matches the height.",
            "Watch the rate of change and accumulation unite.",
            "The Great Loop of Calculus is now complete."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)

        # Colors from Storyboard
        BALLOON_COLOR = "#FF69B4"
        GAUGE_COLOR = "#00FF00"
        CURVE_COLOR = "#FFB6C1"
        
        # Tracker for synchronization (ranges from 0 to 1)
        time_tracker = ValueTracker(0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "The slope of the area graph matches the height."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(GAUGE_COLOR)

        # 1. Gauge (Air Flow Rate) - Visualizes the Derivative
        gauge_box = Rectangle(width=2.4, height=0.5, color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(gauge_box, "A1", "A3")
        gauge_label = Text("Air Flow Rate", font_size=16, color=GAUGE_COLOR).next_to(gauge_box, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        # The filling bar within the gauge
        gauge_bar = Rectangle(width=0.01, height=0.4, color=GAUGE_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.8, stroke_width=0)
        gauge_bar.align_to(gauge_box, LEFT).shift(RIGHT * 0.05)
        
        def update_gauge(m):
            t = time_tracker.get_value()
            # Flow rate function f(t) = sin(pi * t)
            flow_val = np.sin(np.pi * t)
            # Max internal width is approx 2.3
            new_width = max(0.01, flow_val * 2.2)
            m.stretch_to_fit_width(new_width)
            m.align_to(gauge_box, LEFT).shift(RIGHT * 0.05)

        gauge_bar.add_updater(update_gauge)

        # 2. Balloon Character - The physical manifestation of accumulation
        balloon_body = Circle(radius=0.4, color=BALLOON_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.6)
        nozzle = Triangle(color=BALLOON_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.6).scale(0.15).rotate(180*DEGREES).next_to(balloon_body, DOWN, buff=0)
        balloon = VGroup(balloon_body, nozzle)
        self.place_in_area(balloon, "B1", "D3")
        
        def update_balloon(m):
            t = time_tracker.get_value()
            # Volume V(t) = (1/pi) * (1 - cos(pi * t))
            volume = (1/np.pi) * (1 - np.cos(np.pi * t))
            # Scale factor based on radius growth (sqrt of volume in 2D)
            # Starts at 0.7 scale and expands
            growth_scale = 0.8 + 2.2 * np.sqrt(volume)
            m.set_width(growth_scale)
            m.move_to(self.grid["C2"]) # Anchor to central grid point
        
        balloon.add_updater(update_balloon)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(gauge_box), FadeIn(gauge_label), FadeIn(balloon))
        self.add(gauge_bar)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Watch the rate of change and accumulation unite."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(CURVE_COLOR)

        # 3. Volume Curve Graph - Visualizes the Integral
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 1.2, 0.5],
            y_range=[0, 0.8, 0.2],
            x_length=3.0,
            y_length=4.5,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "font_size": 16}
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A4", "F6", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        graph_label = Text("Volume Accumulation", font_size=18, color=CURVE_COLOR).next_to(axes, UP, buff=0.2)
        x_label = Text("Time", font_size=14).next_to(axes.x_axis, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        # Dynamic curve plotting based on tracker
        volume_curve = always_redraw(lambda: axes.plot(
            lambda t: (1/np.pi) * (1 - np.cos(np.pi * t)),
            x_range=[0, max(0.0001, time_tracker.get_value())],
            color=CURVE_COLOR
        ))

        self.play(Create(axes), Write(graph_label), Write(x_label))
        self.add(volume_curve)
        
        # Inflation and Curve Drawing
        self.play(time_tracker.animate.set_value(1.0), run_time=5, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "The Great Loop of Calculus is now complete."
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)

        # 4. Connecting Slope to Rate
        # Demonstrate at t=0.5 where flow is peak
        t_demo = 0.5
        
        # Static graph for tangent line geometry
        static_full_graph = axes.plot(
            lambda t: (1/np.pi) * (1 - np.cos(np.pi * t)),
            x_range=[0, 1],
            color=CURVE_COLOR
        )
        
        # Point and Tangent on the Volume curve
        v_demo = (1/np.pi) * (1 - np.cos(np.pi * t_demo))
        dot = Dot(axes.c2p(t_demo, v_demo), color=WHITE)
        tangent = axes.get_tangent_line(t_demo, static_full_graph, length=2.0, color=GAUGE_COLOR)
        
        slope_info = MathTex(r"\text{Slope} = \text{Flow Rate}", font_size=24, color=GAUGE_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(slope_info, "B5")

        # Arrow linking the physical Flow Rate Gauge to the mathematical Slope
        connection_arrow = Arrow(
            start=self.grid["A2"], # Center of the Gauge area
            end=tangent.get_center(),
            color=GAUGE_COLOR,
            stroke_width=4,
            buff=0.3
        )

        # Move tracker back to demo point to show alignment
        self.play(time_tracker.animate.set_value(t_demo), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(Create(dot), Create(tangent))
        self.play(Write(slope_info), GrowArrow(connection_arrow))
        
        self.wait(3)

outline.content: Define the derivative as the instantaneous rate of change. Explain that by 'zooming in' infinitely on a curve, it looks like a straight line. The derivative tells us the slope of that line at any specific moment (x). Highlight the notation f'(x).
outline.example: A Race Car's speedometer. At exactly 2.5 seconds, the needle points to 60 km/h. That single snapshot of speed is the derivative of the car's position.

storyboard.title: The Derivative: Zooming into 'The Now'
lecture_lines: A derivative represents the instantaneous rate of change.
Zoom into a curve until it looks straight.
This straight line's slope is the derivative f'(x).
Like a speedometer showing speed at one moment.
It captures the precise "steepness of the now."

Place a point on the curve at t=2.5. Display a speedometer (#FF4500) pointing to 60 km/h.
Zoom in on the point at t=2.5 until the curve looks like a straight line (#FFFF00).
Highlight the slope of this line and label it f'(2.5) = 60 (#FFD700).
Fade out the zoom and car ([Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/car.png]); show the general notation f'(x) (#FFFFFF) next to the curve.

            x_length=4.5,

        # [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/car.png] (fading out car here)
        self.play(
            FadeOut(axes), FadeOut(curve), FadeOut(curve_label), FadeOut(car),
            FadeIn(zoomed_axes), FadeIn(zoomed_curve), FadeIn(dot_focus)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # This straight line's slope is the derivative f'(x).
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_SLOPE)

        slope_label = MathTex(r"f^{\prime}(2.5) = 60", color=COLOR_SLOPE).scale(0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(slope_label, "D5")

        self.play(Create(tangent_line))
        self.play(Write(slope_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Like a speedometer showing speed at one moment.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(COLOR_SPEEDO)
        
        # Speedometer visual
        speedo_arc = Arc(radius=0.7, start_angle=PI, angle=-PI, color=GREY).set_stroke(width=4)
        speedo_center = self.grid["B5"]
        speedo_arc.move_to(speedo_center + UP*0.3)
        
        # Needle points up (60 is midpoint in conceptual speedo)
        needle = Line(speedo_arc.get_center(), speedo_arc.get_center() + UP*0.6, color=COLOR_SPEEDO, stroke_width=4)
        
        speedo_val = Text("60 km/h", font_size=16, color=COLOR_SPEEDO)
        speedo_val.next_to(speedo_arc, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        speedo_group = VGroup(speedo_arc, needle, speedo_val)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(speedo_group))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # It captures the precise "steepness of the now."
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(COLOR_TEXT)
        
        # Final notation
        final_notation = MathTex(r"f^{\prime}(x) = \text{slope at } x", color=COLOR_TEXT).scale(1.2)
        self.place_in_area(final_notation, "C2", "E5")
        
        # [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/car.png] (already gone, but following prompt logic)
        self.play(
            FadeOut(zoomed_axes), FadeOut(zoomed_curve), FadeOut(dot_focus), 
            FadeOut(tangent_line), FadeOut(slope_label), FadeOut(speedo_group)
        )
        # Restore background context
        self.add(axes, curve)
        self.play(Write(final_notation))
        self.wait(2)

outline.title: The Fundamental Theorem: The 'Undo' Button
outline.content: Reveal the core secret: Differentiation and Integration are inverse operations, like adding and subtracting. If you have a function representing total distance, its derivative is speed. If you have a function representing speed, its integral is the distance. Graphically, show how the 'area-so-far' function grows based on the height of the original curve.
outline.example: A 3D Printer. The derivative is the 'Extruder' nozzle speed at a specific layer; the integral is the 'Finished Model' created by the accumulation of all those layers.

lecture_lines: Differentiation and integration are inverse operations.

The derivative of distance is your current speed.
The integral of speed is your total distance.
This link is the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus.
animations: Show a 3D printer nozzle (#C0C0C0) moving across a layer. Label its speed as 'Derivative' (#FF8C00).
Show the finished model (#32CD32) growing layer by layer. Label the total model as 'Integral' (#00FA9A).
Display a 'Distance' graph (#FFFFFF) and a 'Speed' graph (#FFD700) stacked vertically.
Animate a point on the Speed graph; show the corresponding Slope of the Distance graph changing.
Display a large 'UNDO' button icon (#FF0000) [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/no.svg] between the symbols d/dx and integral.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4ConnectionScene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Differentiation and integration are inverse operations.",
            "One \"undoes\" the other, like adding and subtracting.",
            "The derivative of distance is your current speed.",
            "The integral of speed is your total distance.",
            "This link is the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Fundamental Theorem: The 'Undo' Button", lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors
        COLOR_DERIVATIVE = "#FF8C00"
        COLOR_INTEGRAL = "#00FA9A"
        COLOR_NOZZLE = "#C0C0C0"
        COLOR_MODEL = "#32CD32"
        COLOR_DISTANCE = "#FFFFFF"
        COLOR_SPEED = "#FFD700"
        COLOR_UNDO = "#FF0000"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        deriv_sym = MathTex(r"\frac{d}{dx}", color=COLOR_DERIVATIVE)
        integ_sym = MathTex(r"\int", color=COLOR_INTEGRAL)
        
        self.place_at_grid(deriv_sym, "A2", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.place_at_grid(integ_sym, "C2", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(deriv_sym), FadeIn(integ_sym))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        undo_box = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, height=0.6, width=1.2, color=COLOR_UNDO, fill_opacity=0.3)
        undo_text = Text("UNDO", font_size=18, color=COLOR_UNDO)
        undo_button = VGroup(undo_box, undo_text)
        self.place_at_grid(undo_button, "B2", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        plus_minus = MathTex(r"+ \longleftrightarrow -", font_size=30, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(plus_minus, "D2", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(undo_button))
        self.play(Write(plus_minus))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(plus_minus))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Symbols stay but fade slightly
        self.play(VGroup(deriv_sym, integ_sym, undo_button).animate.set_opacity(0.3))

        # Graphs
        dist_axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[0, 4, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": False},
            x_length=2.5, y_length=1.5
        ).set_color(COLOR_DISTANCE)
        dist_label = Text("Distance", font_size=16, color=COLOR_DISTANCE)
        dist_vg = VGroup(dist_axes, dist_label).arrange(UP, buff=0.1)
        self.place_in_area(dist_vg, "A4", "C6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        speed_axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[0, 4, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": False},
            x_length=2.5, y_length=1.5
        ).set_color(COLOR_SPEED)
        speed_label = Text("Speed", font_size=16, color=COLOR_SPEED)
        speed_vg = VGroup(speed_axes, speed_label).arrange(UP, buff=0.1)
        self.place_in_area(speed_vg, "D4", "F6", scale_factor=1.0)

        dist_curve = dist_axes.plot(lambda x: x**2 / 4, x_range=[0, 4], color=COLOR_DISTANCE)
        speed_curve = speed_axes.plot(lambda x: x / 2, x_range=[0, 4], color=COLOR_SPEED)

        # 3D Printer Nozzle
        nozzle = Triangle(color=COLOR_NOZZLE, fill_opacity=1.0).scale(0.2).rotate(180*DEGREES)
        nozzle_label = Text("Speed (Deriv.)", font_size=16, color=COLOR_DERIVATIVE)
        nozzle_vg = VGroup(nozzle, nozzle_label).arrange(UP, buff=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(nozzle_vg, "E1", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(Create(dist_axes), Create(speed_axes), FadeIn(dist_label), FadeIn(speed_label))
        self.play(Create(dist_curve), FadeIn(nozzle_vg))
        
        # Derivative linking
        tracker = ValueTracker(0.01)
        
        # Use simple lines and dots for updaters
        slope_line = Line(color=COLOR_DERIVATIVE, stroke_width=4)
        def update_slope_line(line):
            val = tracker.get_value()
            slope = val / 2 # Derivative of x^2/4 is x/2
            p = dist_axes.c2p(val, val**2 / 4)
            # Tangent line segment
            line.set_points_as_corners([p + LEFT*0.5 + DOWN*0.5*slope, p + RIGHT*0.5 + UP*0.5*slope])

        slope_line.add_updater(update_slope_line)
        
        speed_dot = Dot(color=COLOR_SPEED)
        speed_dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(speed_axes.c2p(tracker.get_value(), tracker.get_value()/2)))
        
        self.add(slope_line, speed_dot)
        self.play(
            tracker.animate.set_value(4), 
            Create(speed_curve), 
            nozzle_vg.animate.shift(RIGHT * 1.5), 
            run_time=4, 
            rate_func=linear
        )
        slope_line.clear_updaters()
        speed_dot.clear_updaters()
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Finished Model (Integral)
        model_base = Line(LEFT, RIGHT, color=GREY).scale(0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(model_base, "F2", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        model_rect = Rectangle(height=0.01, width=1.0, color=COLOR_MODEL, fill_opacity=0.8)
        model_rect.move_to(model_base.get_center(), aligned_edge=DOWN)
        
        model_label = Text("Model (Integral)", font_size=16, color=COLOR_INTEGRAL)
        self.place_at_grid(model_label, "F3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Area under speed graph
        area = speed_axes.get_area(speed_curve, x_range=[0, 4], color=COLOR_INTEGRAL, opacity=0.3)
        
        self.play(Create(model_base), FadeIn(model_label), Create(model_rect))
        
        # Growth animation
        tracker.set_value(0.01)
        model_rect.add_updater(lambda m: m.set_height(max(0.01, tracker.get_value() * 0.4), stretch=True).move_to(model_base.get_center(), aligned_edge=DOWN))
        
        self.play(Create(area), tracker.animate.set_value(4), run_time=3)
        model_rect.clear_updaters()
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        ftc_text = Text("Fundamental Theorem of Calculus", font_size=24, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_in_area(ftc_text, "B2", "C5", scale_factor=0.9)
        ftc_box = SurroundingRectangle(ftc_text, color=YELLOW, buff=0.2)
        
        # Highlight everything
        self.play(
            FadeIn(ftc_box), 
            Write(ftc_text), 
            VGroup(deriv_sym, integ_sym, undo_button).animate.set_opacity(1).scale(1.2)
        )
        self.play(Indicate(undo_button, color=COLOR_UNDO), Indicate(ftc_text))
        self.wait(3)

        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]

        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

        return mobject

class Section5SynthesisScene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initial Setup
        title = "Visual Synthesis & Animation"
        lecture_lines = [
            "The slope of the area graph matches the height.",
            "Watch the rate of change and accumulation unite.",
            "The Great Loop of Calculus is now complete."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)

        # Colors from Storyboard
        BALLOON_COLOR = "#FF69B4"
        GAUGE_COLOR = "#00FF00"
        CURVE_COLOR = "#FFB6C1"
        
        # Tracker for synchronization (ranges from 0 to 1)
        time_tracker = ValueTracker(0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "The slope of the area graph matches the height."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(GAUGE_COLOR)

        # 1. Gauge (Air Flow Rate) - Visualizes the Derivative
        gauge_box = Rectangle(width=2.4, height=0.5, color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(gauge_box, "A1", "A3")
        gauge_label = Text("Air Flow Rate", font_size=16, color=GAUGE_COLOR).next_to(gauge_box, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        # The filling bar within the gauge
        gauge_bar = Rectangle(width=0.01, height=0.4, color=GAUGE_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.8, stroke_width=0)
        gauge_bar.align_to(gauge_box, LEFT).shift(RIGHT * 0.05)
        
        def update_gauge(m):
            t = time_tracker.get_value()
            # Flow rate function f(t) = sin(pi * t)
            flow_val = np.sin(np.pi * t)
            # Max internal width is approx 2.3
            new_width = max(0.01, flow_val * 2.2)
            m.stretch_to_fit_width(new_width)
            m.align_to(gauge_box, LEFT).shift(RIGHT * 0.05)

        gauge_bar.add_updater(update_gauge)

        # 2. Balloon Character - The physical manifestation of accumulation
        balloon_body = Circle(radius=0.4, color=BALLOON_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.6)
        nozzle = Triangle(color=BALLOON_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.6).scale(0.15).rotate(180*DEGREES).next_to(balloon_body, DOWN, buff=0)
        balloon = VGroup(balloon_body, nozzle)
        self.place_in_area(balloon, "B1", "D3")
        
        def update_balloon(m):
            t = time_tracker.get_value()
            # Volume V(t) = (1/pi) * (1 - cos(pi * t))
            volume = (1/np.pi) * (1 - np.cos(np.pi * t))
            # Scale factor based on radius growth (sqrt of volume in 2D)
            # Starts at 0.7 scale and expands
            growth_scale = 0.8 + 2.2 * np.sqrt(volume)
            m.set_width(growth_scale)
            m.move_to(self.grid["C2"]) # Anchor to central grid point
        
        balloon.add_updater(update_balloon)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(gauge_box), FadeIn(gauge_label), FadeIn(balloon))
        self.add(gauge_bar)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Watch the rate of change and accumulation unite."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(CURVE_COLOR)

        # 3. Volume Curve Graph - Visualizes the Integral
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 1.2, 0.5],
            y_range=[0, 0.8, 0.2],
            x_length=3.0,
            y_length=4.5,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "font_size": 16}
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A4", "F6", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        graph_label = Text("Volume Accumulation", font_size=18, color=CURVE_COLOR).next_to(axes, UP, buff=0.2)
        x_label = Text("Time", font_size=14).next_to(axes.x_axis, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        # Dynamic curve plotting based on tracker
        volume_curve = always_redraw(lambda: axes.plot(
            lambda t: (1/np.pi) * (1 - np.cos(np.pi * t)),
            x_range=[0, max(0.0001, time_tracker.get_value())],
            color=CURVE_COLOR
        ))

        self.play(Create(axes), Write(graph_label), Write(x_label))
        self.add(volume_curve)
        
        # Inflation and Curve Drawing
        self.play(time_tracker.animate.set_value(1.0), run_time=5, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5SynthesisScene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initial Setup
        title = "Visual Synthesis & Animation"
        lecture_lines = [
            "The slope of the area graph matches the height.",
            "Watch the rate of change and accumulation unite.",
            "The Great Loop of Calculus is now complete."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)

        # Colors from Storyboard
        BALLOON_COLOR = "#FF69B4"
        GAUGE_COLOR = "#00FF00"
        CURVE_COLOR = "#FFB6C1"
        
        # Tracker for synchronization (ranges from 0 to 1)
        time_tracker = ValueTracker(0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "The slope of the area graph matches the height."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(GAUGE_COLOR)

        # 1. Gauge (Air Flow Rate) [Asset: gauge.svg]
        gauge_svg = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/gauge.svg")
        gauge_svg.set_color(GAUGE_COLOR)
        self.place_in_area(gauge_svg, "A1", "A3", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        gauge_label = Text("Air Flow Rate", font_size=16, color=GAUGE_COLOR).next_to(gauge_svg, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        # Adding a visual bar indicator for the flow value next to the gauge
        gauge_bar_bg = Rectangle(width=1.5, height=0.2, color=GRAY, fill_opacity=0.3).next_to(gauge_svg, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        gauge_bar = Rectangle(width=0.01, height=0.2, color=GAUGE_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.8, stroke_width=0)
        gauge_bar.align_to(gauge_bar_bg, LEFT)
        
        def update_gauge(m):
            t = time_tracker.get_value()
            # Flow rate function f(t) = sin(pi * t)
            flow_val = np.sin(np.pi * t)
            new_width = max(0.01, flow_val * 1.5)
            # Use scale_to_fit_width to avoid deprecation and be robust
            m.stretch_to_fit_width(new_width)
            m.align_to(gauge_bar_bg, LEFT)

        gauge_bar.add_updater(update_gauge)

        # 2. Balloon Character [Asset: balloon.svg]
        balloon_svg = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/balloon.svg")
        balloon_svg.set_color(BALLOON_COLOR)
        self.place_in_area(balloon_svg, "B1", "D3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Center point for balloon anchoring
        balloon_center = self.grid["C2"]
        
        def update_balloon(m):
            t = time_tracker.get_value()
            # Volume V(t) = (1/pi) * (1 - cos(pi * t))
            volume = (1/np.pi) * (1 - np.cos(np.pi * t))
            # Base width + growth
            growth_width = 0.5 + 2.0 * np.sqrt(volume)
            m.stretch_to_fit_width(growth_width)
            m.stretch_to_fit_height(growth_width) # Keep aspect ratio roughly
            m.move_to(balloon_center)
        
        balloon_svg.add_updater(update_balloon)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(gauge_svg), FadeIn(gauge_label), FadeIn(gauge_bar_bg), FadeIn(balloon_svg))
        self.add(gauge_bar)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Watch the rate of change and accumulation unite."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(CURVE_COLOR)

        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 1.2, 0.5],
            y_range=[0, 0.8, 0.2],
            x_length=3.0,
            y_length=4.0,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "font_size": 16}
        )
        # Position axes on the right side
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A4", "F6", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        graph_label = Text("Volume (Integral)", font_size=18, color=CURVE_COLOR).next_to(axes, UP, buff=0.2)
        x_label = Text("Time", font_size=14).next_to(axes.x_axis, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        # Dynamic curve plotting
        volume_curve = always_redraw(lambda: axes.plot(
            lambda t: (1/np.pi) * (1 - np.cos(np.pi * t)),
            x_range=[0, max(0.0001, time_tracker.get_value())],
            color=CURVE_COLOR
        ))

        self.play(Create(axes), FadeIn(graph_label), FadeIn(x_label))
        self.add(volume_curve)
        
        # Inflation and Curve Drawing
        self.play(time_tracker.animate.set_value(1.0), run_time=5, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "The Great Loop of Calculus is now complete."
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)

        # 4. Connecting Slope to Rate
        t_demo = 0.5
        v_demo = (1/np.pi) * (1 - np.cos(np.pi * t_demo))
        
        # Static graph for tangent line
        static_full_graph = axes.plot(
            lambda t: (1/np.pi) * (1 - np.cos(np.pi * t)),
            x_range=[0, 1.0],
            color=CURVE_COLOR
        )
        
        # Point on the Volume curve
        dot = Dot(axes.c2p(t_demo, v_demo), color=WHITE)
        
        # Manual Tangent Line to avoid TypeError with get_tangent_line
        # At t=0.5, V'(t) = sin(pi*0.5) = 1.0
        # The slope in plot units is 1.0. 
        # But we need to account for axes scaling: dx=1 unit on x-axis, dy=1 unit on y-axis.
        # Axes c2p does this.
        p1 = axes.c2p(t_demo - 0.25, v_demo - 0.25)
        p2 = axes.c2p(t_demo + 0.25, v_demo + 0.25)
        tangent = Line(p1, p2, color=GAUGE_COLOR, stroke_width=6)
        
        slope_info = Text("Slope = Flow Rate", font_size=18, color=GAUGE_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(slope_info, "B5")

        # Connection Arrow
        connection_arrow = Arrow(
            start=gauge_svg.get_center(),
            end=tangent.get_center(),
            color=GAUGE_COLOR,
            stroke_width=4,
            buff=0.3
        )

        # Move tracker back to demo point
        self.play(time_tracker.animate.set_value(t_demo), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(Create(dot), Create(tangent))
        self.play(FadeIn(slope_info), GrowArrow(connection_arrow))
        
        self.wait(3)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5SynthesisScene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initial Setup
        title = "Visual Synthesis & Animation"
        lecture_lines = [
            "The slope of the area graph matches the height.",
            "Watch the rate of change and accumulation unite.",
            "The Great Loop of Calculus is now complete."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)

        # Colors from Storyboard
        BALLOON_COLOR = "#FF69B4"
        GAUGE_COLOR = "#00FF00"
        CURVE_COLOR = "#FFB6C1"
        
        # Tracker for synchronization (ranges from 0 to 1)
        time_tracker = ValueTracker(0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "The slope of the area graph matches the height."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(GAUGE_COLOR)

        # 1. Gauge (Air Flow Rate) [Asset: gauge.svg]
        gauge_svg = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/gauge.svg")
        gauge_svg.set_color(GAUGE_COLOR)
        self.place_in_area(gauge_svg, "A1", "A3", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        gauge_label = Text("Air Flow Rate", font_size=16, color=GAUGE_COLOR).next_to(gauge_svg, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        # Adding a visual bar indicator for the flow value next to the gauge
        gauge_bar_bg = Rectangle(width=1.5, height=0.2, color=GRAY, fill_opacity=0.3).next_to(gauge_svg, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        gauge_bar = Rectangle(width=0.01, height=0.2, color=GAUGE_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.8, stroke_width=0)
        gauge_bar.align_to(gauge_bar_bg, LEFT)
        
        def update_gauge(m):
            t = time_tracker.get_value()
            # Flow rate function f(t) = sin(pi * t)
            flow_val = np.sin(np.pi * t)
            new_width = max(0.01, flow_val * 1.5)
            # Use stretch_to_fit_width for robust scaling
            m.stretch_to_fit_width(new_width)
            m.align_to(gauge_bar_bg, LEFT)

        gauge_bar.add_updater(update_gauge)

        # 2. Balloon Character [Asset: balloon.svg]
        balloon_svg = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/balloon.svg")
        balloon_svg.set_color(BALLOON_COLOR)
        self.place_in_area(balloon_svg, "B1", "D3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Center point for balloon anchoring
        balloon_center = self.grid["C2"]
        
        def update_balloon(m):
            t = time_tracker.get_value()
            # Volume V(t) = (1/pi) * (1 - cos(pi * t))
            volume = (1/np.pi) * (1 - np.cos(np.pi * t))
            # Base width + growth
            growth_width = 0.5 + 2.0 * np.sqrt(volume)
            m.stretch_to_fit_width(growth_width)
            m.stretch_to_fit_height(growth_width) # Keep aspect ratio roughly
            m.move_to(balloon_center)
        
        balloon_svg.add_updater(update_balloon)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(gauge_svg), FadeIn(gauge_label), FadeIn(gauge_bar_bg), FadeIn(balloon_svg))
        self.add(gauge_bar)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Watch the rate of change and accumulation unite."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(CURVE_COLOR)

        # 3. Volume Curve Graph - Visualizes the Integral
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 1.2, 0.5],
            y_range=[0, 0.8, 0.2],
            x_length=3.0,
            y_length=4.0,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "font_size": 16}
        )
        # Position axes on the right side
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A4", "F6", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        graph_label = Text("Volume (Integral)", font_size=18, color=CURVE_COLOR).next_to(axes, UP, buff=0.2)
        x_label = Text("Time", font_size=14).next_to(axes.x_axis, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        # Dynamic curve plotting
        volume_curve = always_redraw(lambda: axes.plot(
            lambda t: (1/np.pi) * (1 - np.cos(np.pi * t)),
            x_range=[0, max(0.0001, time_tracker.get_value())],
            color=CURVE_COLOR
        ))

        self.play(Create(axes), FadeIn(graph_label), FadeIn(x_label))
        self.add(volume_curve)
        
        # Inflation and Curve Drawing
        self.play(time_tracker.animate.set_value(1.0), run_time=5, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "The Great Loop of Calculus is now complete."
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)

        # 4. Connecting Slope to Rate
        t_demo = 0.5
        v_demo = (1/np.pi) * (1 - np.cos(np.pi * t_demo))
        
        # Static graph for tangent line
        static_full_graph = axes.plot(
            lambda t: (1/np.pi) * (1 - np.cos(np.pi * t)),
            x_range=[0, 1.0],
            color=CURVE_COLOR
        )
        
        # Point on the Volume curve
        dot = Dot(axes.c2p(t_demo, v_demo), color=WHITE)
        
        # Manual Tangent Line to avoid TypeError with get_tangent_line
        # At t=0.5, V'(t) = sin(pi*0.5) = 1.0
        p1 = axes.c2p(t_demo - 0.25, v_demo - 0.25)
        p2 = axes.c2p(t_demo + 0.25, v_demo + 0.25)
        tangent = Line(p1, p2, color=GAUGE_COLOR, stroke_width=6)
        
        slope_info = Text("Slope = Flow Rate", font_size=18, color=GAUGE_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(slope_info, "B5")

        # Connection Arrow
        connection_arrow = Arrow(
            start=gauge_svg.get_center(),
            end=tangent.get_center(),
            color=GAUGE_COLOR,
            stroke_width=4,
            buff=0.3
        )

        # Move tracker back to demo point
        self.play(time_tracker.animate.set_value(t_demo), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(Create(dot), Create(tangent))
        self.play(FadeIn(slope_info), GrowArrow(connection_arrow))
        
        self.wait(3)

outline.title: The Fundamental Theorem: The 'Undo' Button
outline.content: Reveal the core secret: Differentiation and Integration are inverse operations, like adding and subtracting. If you have a function representing total distance, its derivative is speed. If you have a function representing speed, its integral is the distance. Graphically, show how the 'area-so-far' function grows based on the height of the original curve.
outline.example: A 3D Printer. The derivative is the 'Extruder' nozzle speed at a specific layer; the integral is the 'Finished Model' created by the accumulation of all those layers.

storyboard.title: The Fundamental Theorem: The 'Undo' Button
lecture_lines: Differentiation and integration are inverse operations.
One "undoes" the other, like adding and subtracting.
The derivative of distance is your current speed.
The integral of speed is your total distance.
This link is the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus.
animations: Show a 3D printer nozzle (#C0C0C0) moving across a layer. Label its speed as 'Derivative' (#FF8C00).
Show the finished model (#32CD32) growing layer by layer. Label the total model as 'Integral' (#00FA9A).
Display a 'Distance' graph (#FFFFFF) and a 'Speed' graph (#FFD700) stacked vertically.
Animate a point on the Speed graph; show the corresponding Slope of the Distance graph changing.
Display a large 'UNDO' button icon (#FF0000) [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/no.svg] between the symbols d/dx and integral.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4ConnectionScene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Differentiation and integration are inverse operations.",
            "One \"undoes\" the other, like adding and subtracting.",
            "The derivative of distance is your current speed.",
            "The integral of speed is your total distance.",
            "This link is the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Fundamental Theorem: The 'Undo' Button", lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors
        COLOR_DERIVATIVE = "#FF8C00"
        COLOR_INTEGRAL = "#00FA9A"
        COLOR_NOZZLE = "#C0C0C0"
        COLOR_MODEL = "#32CD32"
        COLOR_DISTANCE = "#FFFFFF"
        COLOR_SPEED = "#FFD700"
        COLOR_UNDO = "#FF0000"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # L1: Show a 3D printer nozzle (#C0C0C0) moving across a layer. Label its speed as 'Derivative' (#FF8C00).
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        nozzle = Triangle(color=COLOR_NOZZLE, fill_opacity=1.0).scale(0.2).rotate(180*DEGREES)
        nozzle_label = Text("Derivative (Speed)", font_size=16, color=COLOR_DERIVATIVE)
        nozzle_vg = VGroup(nozzle, nozzle_label).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(nozzle_vg, "B2")
        
        path = Line(self.grid["B1"], self.grid["B5"], color=GREY_E)
        self.add(path)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(nozzle_vg))
        self.play(nozzle_vg.animate.move_to(self.grid["B5"]), run_time=1.5, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # L2: Show the finished model (#32CD32) growing layer by layer. Label the total model as 'Integral' (#00FA9A).
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        model_base = Line(self.grid["E1"], self.grid["E5"], color=GREY_B)
        # Create a rectangle that starts small and grows
        model_rect = Rectangle(width=4.0, height=0.01, color=COLOR_MODEL, fill_opacity=0.8, stroke_width=0)
        model_rect.move_to(model_base.get_center(), aligned_edge=DOWN)
        model_label = Text("Integral (Model)", font_size=16, color=COLOR_INTEGRAL)
        self.place_at_grid(model_label, "F3")
        
        self.play(Create(model_base), FadeIn(model_label))
        self.play(model_rect.animate.stretch_to_fit_height(1.5).move_to(model_base.get_center(), aligned_edge=DOWN), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # L3: Display a 'Distance' graph (#FFFFFF) and a 'Speed' graph (#FFD700) stacked vertically.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(nozzle_vg, path, model_base, model_rect, model_label))

        dist_axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[0, 4, 1],
            x_length=3, y_length=1.5,
            axis_config={"color": WHITE, "include_tip": False}
        ).scale(0.8)
        dist_label = Text("Distance", font_size=14, color=COLOR_DISTANCE)
        dist_vg = VGroup(dist_axes, dist_label).arrange(UP, buff=0.1)
        self.place_in_area(dist_vg, "A4", "B6")

        speed_axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[0, 4, 1],
            x_length=3, y_length=1.5,
            axis_config={"color": COLOR_SPEED, "include_tip": False}
        ).scale(0.8)
        speed_label = Text("Speed", font_size=14, color=COLOR_SPEED)
        speed_vg = VGroup(speed_axes, speed_label).arrange(UP, buff=0.1)
        self.place_in_area(speed_vg, "D4", "E6")

        dist_curve = dist_axes.plot(lambda x: 0.2 * x**2, x_range=[0, 4], color=COLOR_DISTANCE)
        speed_curve = speed_axes.plot(lambda x: 0.4 * x, x_range=[0, 4], color=COLOR_SPEED)

        self.play(Create(dist_axes), Create(speed_axes), FadeIn(dist_label), FadeIn(speed_label))
        self.play(Create(dist_curve), Create(speed_curve))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # L4: Animate a point on the Speed graph; show the corresponding Slope of the Distance graph changing.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        vt = ValueTracker(0.1)
        
        speed_dot = Dot(color=COLOR_SPEED, radius=0.08)
        speed_dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(speed_axes.c2p(vt.get_value(), 0.4 * vt.get_value())))
        
        tangent = Line(LEFT, RIGHT, color=COLOR_DERIVATIVE).scale(0.4)
        def update_tangent(t):
            x = vt.get_value()
            slope = 0.4 * x
            dx = 0.3
            # Use points for robust tangent line update
            p1 = dist_axes.c2p(x - dx, 0.2 * x**2 - slope * dx)
            p2 = dist_axes.c2p(x + dx, 0.2 * x**2 + slope * dx)
            t.set_points_as_corners([p1, p2])

        tangent.add_updater(update_tangent)
        
        self.add(speed_dot, tangent)
        self.play(vt.animate.set_value(3.8), run_time=2.5, rate_func=linear)
        tangent.clear_updaters()
        speed_dot.clear_updaters()
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # L5: This link is the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Fade out graphs slightly to highlight the FTC symbols
        self.play(VGroup(dist_vg, speed_vg, dist_curve, speed_curve, tangent, speed_dot).animate.set_opacity(0.3))

        deriv_sym = Text("d/dx", color=COLOR_DERIVATIVE, font_size=32)
        integ_sym = Text("∫", color=COLOR_INTEGRAL, font_size=40)
        
        # Large 'UNDO' button icon [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/no.svg]
        undo_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/no.svg").set_color(COLOR_UNDO)
        undo_label = Text("UNDO", font_size=14, color=COLOR_UNDO)
        undo_btn = VGroup(undo_icon, undo_label).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        ftc_vg = VGroup(deriv_sym, undo_btn, integ_sym).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.5)
        self.place_in_area(ftc_vg, "B1", "C3")
        
        ftc_title = Text("Fundamental Theorem", font_size=20, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(ftc_title, "A2")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(ftc_title), Write(deriv_sym), Write(integ_sym))
        self.play(FadeIn(undo_btn))
        self.play(Indicate(undo_btn, scale_factor=1.2))
        self.wait(2)

        dist_label = Text("Distance", font_size=14, color=COLOR_DISTANCE)
        dist_vg = VGroup(dist_axes, dist_label).arrange(UP, buff=0.1)
        self.place_in_area(dist_vg, "A4", "B6")

        speed_axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[0, 4, 1],
            x_length=3, y_length=1.5,
            axis_config={"color": COLOR_SPEED, "include_tip": False}
        ).scale(0.8)
        speed_label = Text("Speed", font_size=14, color=COLOR_SPEED)
        speed_vg = VGroup(speed_axes, speed_label).arrange(UP, buff=0.1)
        self.place_in_area(speed_vg, "D4", "E6")

        dist_curve = dist_axes.plot(lambda x: 0.2 * x**2, x_range=[0, 4], color=COLOR_DISTANCE)
        speed_curve = speed_axes.plot(lambda x: 0.4 * x, x_range=[0, 4], color=COLOR_SPEED)

        self.play(Create(dist_axes), Create(speed_axes), FadeIn(dist_label), FadeIn(speed_label))
        self.play(Create(dist_curve), Create(speed_curve))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # L4: Animate a point on the Speed graph; show the corresponding Slope of the Distance graph changing.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        vt = ValueTracker(0.1)
        
        speed_dot = Dot(color=COLOR_SPEED, radius=0.08)
        speed_dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(speed_axes.c2p(vt.get_value(), 0.4 * vt.get_value())))
        
        tangent = Line(LEFT, RIGHT, color=COLOR_DERIVATIVE).scale(0.4)
        def update_tangent(t):
            x = vt.get_value()
            slope = 0.4 * x
            dx = 0.3
            # Use points for robust tangent line update
            p1 = dist_axes.c2p(x - dx, 0.2 * x**2 - slope * dx)
            p2 = dist_axes.c2p(x + dx, 0.2 * x**2 + slope * dx)
            t.set_points_as_corners([p1, p2])

        tangent.add_updater(update_tangent)
        
        self.add(speed_dot, tangent)
        self.play(vt.animate.set_value(3.8), run_time=2.5, rate_func=linear)
        tangent.clear_updaters()
        speed_dot.clear_updaters()
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # L5: This link is the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Fade out graphs slightly to highlight the FTC symbols
        self.play(VGroup(dist_vg, speed_vg, dist_curve, speed_curve, tangent, speed_dot).animate.set_opacity(0.3))

        deriv_sym = Text("d/dx", color=COLOR_DERIVATIVE, font_size=32)
        integ_sym = Text("∫", color=COLOR_INTEGRAL, font_size=40)
        
        # Large 'UNDO' button icon [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/no.svg]
        undo_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/no.svg").set_color(COLOR_UNDO)
        undo_label = Text("UNDO", font_size=14, color=COLOR_UNDO)
        undo_btn = VGroup(undo_icon, undo_label).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        ftc_vg = VGroup(deriv_sym, undo_btn, integ_sym).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.5)
        self.place_in_area(ftc_vg, "B1", "C3")
        
        ftc_title = Text("Fundamental Theorem", font_size=20, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(ftc_title, "A2")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(ftc_title), Write(deriv_sym), Write(integ_sym))
        self.play(FadeIn(undo_btn))
        self.play(Indicate(undo_btn, scale_factor=1.2))
        self.wait(2)

section_1_prerequisites.title: Prerequisite Check: The Slope and the Area
section_1_prerequisites.content: Briefly revisit two core geometric ideas: 1. Slope (steepness of a line) and 2. Area (space inside a shape). Establish that Calculus is just the study of these two ideas applied to curves instead of straight lines. Use a simple line graph to show these concepts side-by-side.
section_1_prerequisites.example: Visualize a Snail climbing a hill. The 'Steepness' is how hard the snail works at a single point; the 'Total Grass Eaten' is the area of the field the snail covered.

section_2_derivative.title: The Derivative: Zooming into 'The Now'
section_2_derivative.content: Define the derivative as the instantaneous rate of change. Explain that by 'zooming in' infinitely on a curve, it looks like a straight line. The derivative tells us the slope of that line at any specific moment (x). Highlight the notation f'(x).
section_2_derivative.example: A Race Car's speedometer. At exactly 2.5 seconds, the needle points to 60 km/h. That single snapshot of speed is the derivative of the car's position.

section_3_integral.title: The Integral: Accumulating the 'Whole'
section_3_integral.content: Define the definite integral as the total accumulation or the 'Area Under the Curve'. Explain the process of 'Slicing': dividing a complex shape into infinitely many thin rectangles and summing them up. Highlight the notation ∫ f(x) dx.
section_3_integral.example: A Rain Gauge collecting water. If the rain falls at different rates (the curve), the total water in the bucket at the end of the hour is the integral of the rainfall rate.

section_4_connection.title: The Fundamental Theorem: The 'Undo' Button
section_4_connection.content: Reveal the core secret: Differentiation and Integration are inverse operations, like adding and subtracting. If you have a function representing total distance, its derivative is speed. If you have a function representing speed, its integral is the distance. Graphically, show how the 'area-so-far' function grows based on the height of the original curve.
section_4_connection.example: A 3D Printer. The derivative is the 'Extruder' nozzle speed at a specific layer; the integral is the 'Finished Model' created by the accumulation of all those layers.

section_5_synthesis.title: Visual Synthesis & Animation
section_5_synthesis.content: Animate a point moving along a curve. Simultaneously show two graphs: one tracking the 'Slope' (Derivative) and one filling in the 'Area' (Integral). Demonstrate that the 'Slope' of the Area graph is equal to the 'Height' of the original graph.
section_5_synthesis.example: A 'Balloon Character' inflating. The 'Rate of Air Flow' (Derivative) determines how fast the 'Volume' (Integral) increases. If the flow stops (Derivative = 0), the volume stays constant (Integral curve becomes a flat line).

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1PrerequisitesScene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard
        title = "Prerequisite Check: The Slope and the Area"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Calculus studies slope and area applied to curves.",
            "Slope measures the steepness at a single point.",
            "Area measures the space accumulated under the curve."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors
        COLOR_HILL = "#00FF00"
        COLOR_SNAIL = "#FFFFFF"
        COLOR_SLOPE = "#FFD700"
        COLOR_AREA = "#90EE90"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Line 1: Calculus studies slope and area applied to curves.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_HILL))
        
        # Create a container VGroup for the hill elements to position them together
        # Hill curve: local parabola y = -0.5*(x-2)^2 + 1
        hill_curve = ParametricFunction(
            lambda t: np.array([t, -0.5 * (t - 2)**2 + 1, 0]),
            t_range=[0, 4],
            color=COLOR_HILL
        )
        
        # Snail (visual representation as a Dot with a label)
        snail = Dot(color=COLOR_SNAIL, radius=0.15)
        snail.move_to(hill_curve.point_from_proportion(0.25)) # Position on the curve
        
        # Group and position in the right-side area
        hill_vgroup = VGroup(hill_curve, snail)
        self.place_in_area(hill_vgroup, "B1", "E6", scale_factor=1.1)
        
        snail_label = Text("Snail", font_size=18, color=COLOR_SNAIL)
        # Place label near the snail's expected location (B2/C2)
        self.place_at_grid(snail_label, "B2", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Create(hill_curve))
        self.play(FadeIn(snail), Write(snail_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Line 2: Slope measures the steepness at a single point.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_SLOPE))
        
        # Tangent at snail's position
        tangent_line = TangentLine(hill_curve, alpha=0.25, length=2, color=COLOR_SLOPE)
        
        slope_label = Text("Slope", font_size=24, color=COLOR_SLOPE)
        # Place label in adjacent grid cell C2
        self.place_at_grid(slope_label, "C2", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Create(tangent_line))
        self.play(Write(slope_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Line 3: Area measures the space accumulated under the curve.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_AREA))
        
        # Create area fill under the curve
        # Curve ends are at the same height (y=-1 locally)
        area_pts = [hill_curve.point_from_proportion(p) for p in np.linspace(0, 1, 30)]
        bottom_y = area_pts[0][1]
        bottom_right_corner = np.array([area_pts[-1][0], bottom_y, 0])
        bottom_left_corner = np.array([area_pts[0][0], bottom_y, 0])
        
        area_fill = Polygon(
            *area_pts, 
            bottom_right_corner, 
            bottom_left_corner, 
            color=COLOR_AREA, 
            fill_opacity=0.3, 
            stroke_width=0
        )
        
        area_label = Text("Area", font_size=24, color=COLOR_AREA)
        # Place label inside the shaded area at D4
        self.place_at_grid(area_label, "D4", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(area_fill))
        self.play(Write(area_label))
        self.wait(2)

import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):

        self.lecture[4].set_color(COLOR_TEXT)

        self.wait(2)
